- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate early spikes; reduce forecast magnitude by 15–30% for first 5–7 days after sentiment shift.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) mid-history, model often underestimates subsequent sharp rises; apply upward bias of 20–40% to later forecast days (especially 10–25).
- Model frequently over-anticipates mean reversion after high sentiment peaks; delay peak forecast by 3–5 days and reduce amplitude by 20–35%.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and history shows volatility, model underestimates volatility; scale forecast by 1.2–1.5x for days with high variance in history.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-stage sentiment-driven surges; add 10–25% tail bias to final 5–7 days if sentiment >0.67 in last 3–5 days.
- If model shows “overshoot” after a spike (forecast > true for 2+ consecutive days), apply decay factor of 0.85–0.95 to subsequent forecasts to avoid momentum bias.
